investigation.root_cause: GXGeneratedPage.addUserExits() (GXGeneratedPage.ts:88-91) calls this.userExitsEventThrower.clearEventListeners() unconditionally before adding the caller's user-exit implementation. clearEventListeners() (user-exits-event-thrower.service.ts:29) destructively empties the _userExitsList array — removing ALL previously registered listeners from the root-scoped singleton. Since UserExitsEventThrowerService is application-wide, any GXGeneratedPage subclass that calls addUserExits() silently removes all security and audit hooks registered by other parts of the application. There is no per-component scoping, no restore mechanism, and no notification of displaced listeners.
investigation.attack_scenario:
Insider Threat (Malicious Developer): Attacker creates a GXGeneratedPage subclass that calls addUserExits(new MaliciousUserExits()). The MaliciousUserExits implementation captures preConnect authHeader (credential), postConnect token, and all sendKey data. Upon component activation, all legitimate security hooks (e.g., LifecycleUserExits audit hooks) are silently cleared and replaced. For the remainder of the session, all lifecycle events go exclusively to the malicious implementation. Credentials and terminal data are exfiltrated.

Accidental Displacement: A legitimate developer creates a generated page component and calls addUserExits() not realizing it clears global state. Security monitoring stops working for all users who navigate to that page, without any error or warning.
prerequisites: Attacker must have source code access and ability to deploy a custom GXGeneratedPage subclass
The malicious generated page component must be loaded/instantiated during a user session
Knowledge of the IUserExits interface and the generated page extensibility mechanism

privilege_boundary.start_privilege: Developer with code repository and deployment access
privilege_boundary.achieved_privilege: Ability to disable all security lifecycle hooks and capture session credentials + terminal data

impact.description: Security lifecycle hook displacement allows: (1) silent removal of all audit/monitoring user exits, (2) installation of credential-capturing hooks via VULN-005 (preConnect receives authHeader). The confidentiality impact is low-medium as it requires developer-level deployment access; the risk is more architectural — security controls can be silently removed by any generated page component.

sources: GXGeneratedPage subclass (customer-written or ApplinX-generated code component)
transformations: All subsequent firePreConnect, firePostConnect, firePreSendKey events go to malicious impl
sinks: Malicious IUserExits.postConnect() — receives CreateSessionResponse including Bearer token
Malicious IUserExits.preSendKey/postSendKey — receives all keystrokes and screen responses

direct.impact: Unconditional global listener clear — attack vector
Destructive global operation — should be scoped to component lifecycle

indirect.component: LifecycleUserExits / any security monitoring user exit
indirect.impact: Silently displaced; security audit events stop being processed
Malicious displacement enables credential capture via preConnect authHeader

remediation_guidance.recommended_fix: Remove the clearEventListeners() call from addUserExits(). Implement component-lifecycle-scoped user-exit registration: listeners added by a GXGeneratedPage component should be automatically unregistered when the component is destroyed (ngOnDestroy). Use a Map<component_id, IUserExits[]> instead of a flat list to scope listeners per component.
defense_in_depth: Remove clearEventListeners() from addUserExits() — change to append-only
Tie user-exit registration to component lifecycle (add in ngOnInit, remove in ngOnDestroy)
Log all clearEventListeners() calls with stack trace for audit purposes
Require code review of all GXGeneratedPage subclasses that call addUserExits()
Add CI lint rule: flag any direct calls to clearEventListeners() outside of designated initialization
